keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Epirus row before the Despotate of Epirus (1206). Molossia, the first centralized state in Epirus 'from about 370 BC onwards', is drawn as a 45 km disc round Ioannina (5,817 km2). The page gives no area ('only describes borders': Aetolian League south, Thessaly and Upper Macedonia east, Illyrian tribes north), so the infobox comparison is impossible. Alexander I was installed by Philip II in 343/2 (vassal events).

region.text: Molossia, the heartland of the Molossian state around Ioannina

ledger.note: ~370: the Molossian Aeacidae found the first centralized state in Epirus. 'The Molossian Aeacidae dynasty managed to create the first centralized state in Epirus from about 370 BC onwards'; the earliest known decrees of the Molossian state are dated '370-368 BC'. The page names the dynasty and the date; the land is the researcher's reading (Molossia round Ioannina).

region.text: Molossia, the heartland of the Molossian state around Ioannina

ledger.note: 343/2: Philip II makes Alexander king of Epirus. 'In 343/2 Philip dethroned Arybbas and made Alexander, still in his late 20s, king of Epirus.' Read as a Macedonian client kingship; the page does not use the word vassal.
334: Alexander of Epirus crosses to Italy 'at the request of the Greek colony of Taras' and takes Heraclea from the Lucanians. The page dates the landing, not the captures; the year is a bridge.
334: Terina from the Bruttii ('He then took Heraclea from the Lucanians, Terina from the Bruttii, and Sipontum on the Adriatic coast').

ledger.counterpart: Italic tribes (not named on the page)
ledger.note: 334: Sipontum on the Adriatic coast; the page does not name the owner (Italic tribes).

331: Alexander of Epirus 'was compelled to engage under unfavourable circumstances in the Battle of Pandosia and was killed by a Lucanian'. The page does not say what became of the Italian towns; they are dropped with him (bridging).

region.text: Molossia, the heartland of the Molossian state around Ioannina

ledger.note: 331: the Macedonian-installed king dies; the page says nothing of Epirus's later relation to Macedon (bridging end of the client relation).

region.text: Epirus, the united Epirote state of 330

ledger.note: 330: the Epirote tribes unite. 'Epirote tribes established united political entity: 330 BC'; 'the term Epirus appears as a single political unit in the ancient Greek records for the first time'; Passaron becomes the capital of the united kingdom.
295: Pyrrhus moves the capital from Passaron to Ambracia. 'In 295 BC, Pyrrhus transferred the capital of his kingdom to' Ambracia (infobox 'Ambracia (295-224 BC)').

ledger.counterpart: Ambracia (previous holder not named on the page)
ledger.note: 295: Ambracia is in the kingdom (the capital is moved there). The page does not say how Pyrrhus came by it, or from whom.

region.text: Pyrrhus's half of Macedonia (West Macedonia, read from the page)

ledger.note: 288: Pyrrhus shares Macedonia. 'He co-ruled Macedon together with Lysimachus after driving out Demetrius in 288 BC'; 'they decided to share rulership over Macedonia'. The page gives no partition (the half drawn is the researcher's reading).

region.text: Pyrrhus's half of Macedonia (West Macedonia, read from the page)

ledger.note: 284: Lysimachus drives Pyrrhus out. 'In 284 BC, Lysimachus invaded Pyrrhus's half of Macedonia with a huge army'; 'he was driven out of Macedon by Lysimachus'.

280: Pyrrhus lands in Italy at Tarentum's request ('The Tarentines asked Pyrrhus to lead their war against the Romans' ... 'arrived in Italy in 280 BC'). The page says only that after Beneventum 'Only the city of Tarentum remained under the dominion of the Epirotes'; the start of the dominion is not dated.
277: Pyrrhus takes Eryx in Sicily. 'In 277 BC, Pyrrhus captured the Carthaginian fortress in Eryx, Sicily.'
275: Beneventum ends the Italian and Sicilian adventure. Pyrrhus 'lost all his gains after the Battle of Beneventum in 275 BC'; Eryx is read as one of them (the page names no year for its loss).

region.text: the Macedonian kingdom seized from Antigonus Gonatas

ledger.note: 274: Pyrrhus seizes the Macedonian throne. 'Pyrrhus seized the Macedonian throne from Antigonus II Gonatas in 274 BC and invaded the Peloponnese in 272 BC.' The extent is the researcher's reading.

region.text: the Macedonian kingdom seized from Antigonus Gonatas

ledger.note: 272: Pyrrhus is killed in a street battle at Argos ('Pyrrhus was killed during a street battle at Argos'); the page does not say when Antigonus recovered Macedonia (bridging).
272: Pyrrhus dies; the page is silent on the end of Tarentum's dominion (bridging).

231: the monarchy is abolished and Epirus becomes a federal republic. Infobox 'Monarchy abolished: 231 BC'; text: 'In 233 BC, the last surviving member of the Aeacid royal house, Deidamia, was murdered' and Epirus was 'unified under the auspices of the Epirote League as a federal state with its own parliament (or synedrion)'.
After the monarchy: 'the Aetolians seized Ambracia, Amphilochia, and land north of the Ambracian Gulf.' The page gives no year; 231 is bridged from the end of the monarchy.
224: the capital moves to Phoenice. Infobox 'Phoenice (224-167 BC)'; the text puts it after 233.

notes: Written as the whole life of the Epirote state (370-167), although this group's scope ends with Alexander the Great's death, because the three pages opened cover the whole life. Pages are thin on territory: no area, no frontier. Molossia is drawn as a 45 km disc round Ioannina (5,817 km2) before the 330 union, which is the researcher's reading; the gazetteer's Epirus (12,392 km2) includes southern Albania. The 288 half of Macedonia and the 274 Macedonian land are readings (West Macedonia; 'Ancient Macedon'); Pyrrhus's Italian and Sicilian conquests (Tarentum, Eryx) are small ledger discs not drawn in the keyframes. The Aetolian gains after 231 (Ambracia, Amphilochia) and 'Western Acarnania became independent' are undated on the page (confidence 1); the Acarnanian loss is not an event because the page gives the region no extent. The page conflicts with itself: monarchy abolished 231 (infobox) or Deidamia murdered 233 (text); Pyrrhus's reign 297-272, 307-302 (infobox) or 295 (text); Phoenice from 224 (infobox) or after 233 (text). Gazetteer names used that it lacks: Arta, Policoro, Lamezia Terme, Manfredonia, Erice (places). Counterparts without dossiers: Epirote tribes, Bruttii, Ambracia's earlier holder.
